text: Swimming is a unique form of exercise that utilizes the whole body, leveraging both propulsion and stabilization simultaneously. The basic movements of swimming involve a powerful kick, generating momentum in the water, and then the arm strokes, which control direction and speed. When kicking, beginners often start with a flutter kick, which is a rapid, up-and-down motion, but as they gain strength and confidence, they can transition to a more powerful dolphin kick. Breathing, an essential part of the swimming process, comes later as the technique progresses. Initially, it is recommended to practice breathing while holding your breath in the water, which can help build lung capacity and improve coordination. Over time and as you become more comfortable in the water, you can incorporate full breaths, inhaling and exhaling naturally as you swim.
